answer: A new identity should start on probation, like a small boat tied at the jetty while the ocean tests it. During probation it may only take low-value jobs, and promotion needs approval from a rotating jury of unrelated incumbents who watched its real work for weeks. Jurors stake their own standing on each approval: if the promoted identity is later proven to be one operator's duplicate, approvers lose standing too. A gale scattering cheap copies cannot flood the economy, because each fake must survive slow probation and fool a fresh jury, while one detection punishes those who vouched.
